_comment: Tunable engine config. Scoring weights are calibrated by backtest.py.
_goal_comment: The two settings that matter. 'min_expected_listing_gain_pct' is your goal: the listing gain you are aiming for. 'min_confidence' is how sure the engine must be before it interrupts you, as a probability that the goal is met. Base rate across 156 past listings is 43%, so 0.60 means clearly better than average. Raise the goal for a bigger payoff at a lower hit rate; raise the confidence for fewer, stronger alerts. Any goal works without refitting - the probability is read from what similar past issues actually did.
_capital_comment: The two inputs that drive the application plan. budget_inr gates reach (SME lots run Rs 1.1-1.5 L against ~Rs 15k mainboard); pan_count gates odds and is the stronger lever. pan_count must be PANs you can genuinely fund - ASBA blocks money in each applicant's own bank account.

scoring._curve_comment: Median listing-day gain by FINAL total subscription, fitted on 156 issues that listed between May 2025 and Nov 2026 (rank correlation +0.715). Points are bucket geometric midpoints; the curve interpolates in log space. Medians not means: the mean at 100x+ is +50% against a +37% median because a few issues double. Mainboard-dominated - SME is thinly represented, so SME carries its own risk discount and lower confidence. Refit with: python backtest.py subscription
scoring._blend_comment: GMP and subscription are two estimates of the same thing, so they are averaged, never added - adding would double-count the demand both reflect. subscription_weight is a prior: the subscription side is measured, the GMP side is not, and forward calibration should move this. The maturity factors exist because the curve is fitted on FINAL books; a day-one book is mostly empty and would otherwise drag every estimate to zero.
scoring._composition_comment: Thresholds measured against 156 listed issues, and measured WITHIN subscription buckets - pooling hides the effect. Pooled, NII leverage showed a gap of 0.0pp and looked worthless; inside each bucket it runs -10 to -25pp, a textbook Simpson's paradox, because leveraged books are also big books. QIB lag behaves the same way: -1.5pp pooled at 1-5x rising to -16.8pp at 100x+. Penalties here are deliberately far below the measured separation, since the top buckets hold only 1-3 cases each and the curve already prices book size.

_probability_comment: neighbours = how many similar past issues to read the odds from; 30 of ~156 is a workable trade-off between a local answer and a stable one. Below min_history the engine has too little to quote odds and falls back to the point estimate.
